page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong compute capabilities. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 10 percent, alongside strong multi-core performance in the top 25 percent. Passmark metrics confirm this profile, with CPU, physics, and encryption tests all placing in the top 25 percent. Memory performance is also robust, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25 percent, while uncached memory read and write bandwidths remain in the middle 50 percent. In text generation tasks using a small 135M LLM model, the server delivers top-tier performance of 339.19 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a dense allocation of 32 vCPUs and NVMe storage at a competitive resource-to-compute ratio, though the shared CPU allocation model represents a potential performance consistency tradeoff under sustained peak loads compared to dedicated instances. This configuration is suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, web serving, database operations, and lightweight LLM text generation workloads.
